note: Live-session recording of the screen scenes (series/tools/rec). prepare/teardown run on the laptop, not recorded; commands are typed and run for real. Prepare statements run in one PowerShell session with the episode folder as current directory; variables do not survive into the screens, so each screen re-derives what it needs.
prepare: # owner signs in: az login as labadmin, then the Azure DevOps sign-in; the organization name is typed on the laptop only (never in a file): $env:MG_ADO_ORG = '<organization>'
az devops project create --name $proj --visibility private --source-control git --organization "https://dev.azure.com/$org" --output none

# owner, in the browser: Artifacts > Create Feed 'contoso-packages' (scope Project, upstream sources off); Feed settings > Permissions: add 'Project Collection Build Service' and 'contoso-packages-demo Build Service' as Feed Publisher (Contributor)
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\work | Out-Null; Remove-Item C:\work\orders-app, C:\work\orders-report -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
git config user.name 'Alex Demo'; git config user.email 'alex.demo@contoso.com'
git add -A; git commit -m 'chore: import orders api'; git push -u origin main

az pipelines create --name orders-contracts --repository orders-app --repository-type tfsgit --branch main --yml-path /azure-pipelines.yml --skip-first-run true --organization "https://dev.azure.com/$org" --project $proj --output none
# owner: run the pipeline once (warm-up, not recorded) and click Permit for the feed if asked; expect both jobs green and Contoso.Orders.Contracts 1.0.0 in the feed
az pipelines run --name orders-contracts --branch main --organization "https://dev.azure.com/$org" --project $proj --output none
# owner signs in through the credential provider (browser or device flow)

screens.name: audit
commands: # dotnet nuget why draws its tree only on a real console, so it is started with its own console handles
screens.note: Expected: warning NU1903 for Newtonsoft.Json 10.0.1 (GHSA-5crp-9r3c-p9vr), then error NU1903 as an error with AuditPipeline, then the tree Microsoft.AspNet.WebApi.Client (v5.2.9) -> Newtonsoft.Json (v10.0.1), then 'HIGH Newtonsoft.Json 10.0.1 ... transitive'. Optional capture: dotnet package update --vulnerable. Show Directory.Packages.props in VS Code beside the terminal.

screens.name: auditjob
prepare: git add -A; git commit -m 'feat(orders): add legacy client'; git push -u origin feat/legacy-client
az pipelines run --name orders-contracts --branch feat/legacy-client --organization "https://dev.azure.com/$org" --project $proj --output none
steps: Open the pipeline orders-contracts and the run of branch feat/legacy-client (pushed by prepare)

Run summary: the build job green with a warning (the Package audit step annotated 'Newtonsoft.Json 10.0.1 has a known high severity vulnerability'), the audit job red with 'error NU1903' in the 'Restore with audit as errors' step
Note that the package pushed from the branch is 1.0.0-ci.<build id>, a pre-release

In C:\work\orders-app add the pin to Directory.Packages.props (ItemGroup Label 'Pinned transitive packages', Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.4), dotnet restore (regenerates the lock files), commit, push, Run pipeline again on the branch
mask: Azure DevOps organization name in the browser address bar, pkgs.dev.azure.com URLs and the account menu
labadmin e-mail in the account menu
never show nuget.config with the real organization (use the placeholder copy or the masking command)

screens.name: consume
commands: # map Contoso.* to the wrong source: the package can no longer be found
screens.note: Expect 'line 3: total: total must be greater than zero', 'line 4: customer: customer is required (max 100 characters)', '2 invalid', then error NU1101 'No packages exist with this id in source(s): nuget.org'. The masking filters replace the organization name in anything that is printed; check the first restore output for the feed URL and mask it in the edit if it shows. Optional NU1507 check: remove the packageSourceMapping section and restore.

screens.name: publish
steps: Open the main run of orders-contracts: the 'Authenticate to Azure Artifacts' and 'Push to the feed' steps green; expand 'Push to the feed': 'Pushing Contoso.Orders.Contracts.1.0.0.nupkg to ...' (mask the URL) and 'Your package was pushed.'
Artifacts > contoso-packages: Contoso.Orders.Contracts with versions 1.0.0 and 1.0.0-ci.<id> (from the feat/legacy-client run)

Use Run new on main with no new commit (Rerun failed jobs is not enough): the push step ends with a warning for the existing version ('409 (Conflict ...)') and the job succeeds; capture the exact text
Optional off camera: remove --skip-duplicate on a branch and note the failure message
mask: Azure DevOps organization name in the browser address bar, pkgs.dev.azure.com URLs and the account menu
labadmin e-mail in the account menu
never show nuget.config with the real organization (use the placeholder copy or the masking command)

teardown: # owner: Artifacts > contoso-packages > Feed settings > Delete feed, then Deleted Feeds > Permanently Delete Feed (deleted feeds keep using storage for 30 days)

$pid2 = az devops project show --project $proj --organization "https://dev.azure.com/$org" --query id -o tsv; if ($pid2) { az devops project delete --id $pid2 --organization "https://dev.azure.com/$org" --yes }
Set-Location C:\work; Remove-Item C:\work\orders-app, C:\work\orders-report -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
# owner: check Organization settings > Billing / Artifacts storage the next day (back to 0 GiB, can take 48 hours)
